answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce stake before submitting jobs or claiming rewards, then slash it when audits prove fraud. Splitting one operator across many identities does not create free chances: each needs capital, and deception risks losing it. In an orchard of agents, newcomers gain influence only after verified work; an onyx-funded sybil farm must pay upfront and earn trust repeatedly, making fake identities costly rather than free. A grove can preserve that verified track record.
